Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (Series parquet persistence, struct field extraction), pain points (pyarrow workaround friction), and acceptance criteria (success metrics, edge cases, schema handling). Questions decompose the two linked requirements (Issue #54638 and struct accessor) into concrete user workflows and prioritization drivers.

Generated 12 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (Series Parquet writing, struct field access), pain points (DataFrame-only limitation, PyArrow workaround complexity), and acceptance criteria (metadata preservation, nested schema support, performance). Questions decompose complex requirements into concrete workflows and prioritization context per BABOK v3 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards.

End users require native pandas support for Series.to_parquet() and struct field accessors to eliminate PyArrow workarounds, streamline nested data handling, and enable efficient ETL workflows without forced DataFrame conversions.

End users require symmetric Series.to_parquet() functionality and native struct field accessor to eliminate PyArrow workarounds, reduce API cognitive load, and maintain workflow continuity when handling nested/hierarchical data formats common in modern data processing pipelines.

End users require native Series.to_parquet() export and struct accessor field() methods to eliminate PyArrow workarounds, reduce ETL development time by 15-20%, maintain API consistency, and enable seamless nested data processing workflows in pandas.

Six clarification questions raised regarding Series.to_parquet() parameter parity, struct accessor behavior (index preservation, null handling, nested access), schema inference, performance considerations, and error handling for struct field access to resolve ambiguities in the dual-requirement enhancement (Issue #54638 and struct accessor functionality).

Six critical clarifications needed to resolve ambiguities in Series.to_parquet() parameter compatibility, struct accessor null-handling semantics, nested field access scope, index preservation behavior, engine independence, and dtype consistency before detailed design can proceed.

Seven clarification questions raised addressing Series.to_parquet() parameter scope and index handling, struct accessor null/missing data semantics, nested field access depth, type inference behavior, and error handling—all critical for consistent API design and production pipeline reliability.

End-user confirms two interconnected requirements: (1) Series.to_parquet() with full DataFrame parameter parity to eliminate ETL workarounds, and (2) struct accessor field() method with NA-preserving behavior for nested data access. Recommend Phase 1 single-level struct support with Phase 2 nested dotted-notation. Both features address documented productivity losses and workflow friction in modern data pipelines.

End-user requirements validated and refined: Series.to_parquet() with full parameter parity and struct accessor field() method with index preservation and NA handling confirmed as Phase 1 scope; nested struct access via dotted notation deferred to Phase 2 based on adoption metrics. Both requirements directly address ETL workflow inefficiencies and nested data handling friction in current pandas workflows.

EndUser confirms two critical enhancements: (1) Series.to_parquet() with full symmetric DataFrame API support addressing 15-20% ETL time waste; (2) Struct accessor field() method with index preservation and NA-handling strategy. Phase 1 limited to single-level field extraction with nested access deferred to Phase 2. Both requirements validated as essential for eliminating PyArrow context-switching overhead and maintaining workflow continuity.

Consolidated 6 structured interview records from EndUser dialogue addressing two interconnected feature requirements: (1) Series.to_parquet() export with full DataFrame API parity to eliminate ETL conversion overhead, and (2) struct accessor with field() method for native nested data access. All requirements validated with confirmed scope, phased implementation strategy (Phase 1: single-level struct access; Phase 2: nested dotted notation), and explicit NA handling semantics. Synthesized 8 hierarchical user requirements (1 MUST, 6 MUST, 1 SHOULD, 1 COULD) addressing two critical pandas enhancements: (1) Series.to_parquet() export with symmetric DataFrame API parity including compression/engine/index parameters, and (2) struct accessor field() method with index preservation and NA handling. All MUST requirements validated through enduser confirmations; SHOULD deferred to Phase 2 per adoption metrics; traceability established to interview records, pain points, and clarifications resolved. Chain-of-Thought: Decomposed complex requirements by separating core functionality (REQ-001, 003) from parameter scope (REQ-002, 004) and edge-case handling (REQ-005, 006), then stratified by MoSCoW priority based on enduser validation signals and lifecycle trade-offs (Phase 1 single-level struct access vs. Phase 2 nested notation).

Deployer-focused dialogue probing infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, PyArrow pinning), security mandates (data classification, encryption, audit logging), scalability expectations (Series size, struct depth, throughput), performance SLAs (latency targets, parallelization), backwards compatibility (feature flags, deprecation), and operational readiness (testing infrastructure, monitoring) to ground Series.to_parquet() and struct accessor implementation decisions in production deployment realities.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing infrastructure constraints (PyArrow compatibility, deployment topology, data volumes), security mandates (encryption, compliance, audit logging for sensitive struct fields), and scalability expectations (concurrency models, lazy evaluation, SLA requirements, backward compatibility) to ground Phase 1 implementation scope and validate symmetric API parity strategy for Series.to_parquet() and struct accessor field() method.

Deploy Series.to_parquet() with symmetric DataFrame API parity (compression, engine, index parameters) and struct accessor field() method with single-level extraction, index preservation, and NA-handling guarantees. Validate against PyArrow 10.0+, enforce path/field-name security, support 1B+ row scalability via lazy evaluation, document Phase 1 scope limitations, and provide optional-dependency flexibility for cost control.

Deployer constraints address PyArrow/fastparquet dependency management with CI/CD validation across platforms, memory-efficient struct field extraction for 100M+ row datasets, path traversal security in parquet export, streaming writes for scalability, compression cost optimization, and clear operational error handling with phased feature roadmap documentation.

Deployer constraints mandate PyArrow ≥10.0 as optional dependency with cross-engine CI/CD validation, strict path traversal security (whitelist + sanitization), and performance scalability (<5s for 100M-row field extraction). Operational procedures include pre-deployment security audits, post-deployment regression monitoring, and graceful degradation when engines unavailable. Cost-performance optimization via lazy imports and tuned compression defaults balances footprint/speed tradeoffs.
